name: Sarcasm
overview: Scripture presents sarcasm as a form of speech that often reveals deeper spiritual or moral truths through pointed irony and reproach. For example, Cain’s retort to God, "Am I my brother's keeper?" (Genesis 4:9), exposes his self-justifying hardness of heart, while the Israelites’ bitter question to Moses, accusing him of leading them to death in the wilderness (Exodus 14:11), reflects their distrust and rebellion. Joshua’s challenge to the descendants of Joseph (Joshua 17:15) uses sarcasm to confront their complacency, and Jotham’s public address (Judges 9:7) employs sharp irony to warn the men of Shechem. These instances demonstrate how sarcasm in Scripture often serves to expose sin, provoke repentance, or highlight folly under God’s sovereign judgment.
